messages:
sam: Heads-up 1 I just opened a docs PR for the on-prem installer migration guide that covers: switching PKCS#11 providers, IPv6 dual-stack firewall examples, and offline bundle changes. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4278
tess-docs: Nice. Can you call out exact pkcs11 URIs we recommend for common HSMs? Also need a compact upgrade checklist so SREs can follow without reading the whole page.
raul: For URIs, minimal examples: `pkcs11:token=acme;object=bastion-key` and `pkcs11:slot-id=1;object=server-cert`. Add note that some HSMs use labels vs object IDs.
kevin: On the dual-stack bit: customers keep tripping over ip6tables vs nftables differences. Want a tiny nftables example that includes both ip and ip6 families?
sam: Yes, please. Keep it small. Also include sysctl toggles for forwarding and accept_ra behavior.
raul: Draft nftables snippet (ip + ip6):
```
# minimal nftables for proxy host (ipv4 + ipv6)
flush ruleset

table inet filter {
  chain input { type filter hook input priority 0; ct state established,related accept; iifname "lo" accept; tcp dport {443} accept; }
  chain forward { type filter hook forward priority 0; }
}

# ensure ip_forward for v4 and v6
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
```

Add `net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra=0` if you want static routes only.
tess-docs: Good. Can you also add a tiny ip6tables-only snippet for folks not on nftables? Keep it 3 lines.
raul: Sure: `ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT` plus `ip6tables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT`.
kevin: For the offline bundle section, we should recommend bundling the PKCS#11 provider packages and the correct kernel module versions. Also add the signature verification step.
sam: Security wants a stronger line about verifying artifacts.
sec: Please include: "Verify GPG signatures on all offline packages and check SHA256 sums before installation. Never skip verification in air-gapped installs." Keep it short.
tess-docs: We'll add one-liner examples for verification: `gpg --verify provider.rpm.sig provider.rpm` and `sha256sum -c provider.sha256`.
raul: Also add a migration checklist (compact 6 steps):
- Backup HSM config and export ACLs (if supported)
- Confirm PKCS#11 labels/IDs for keys used by proxy and services
- Stage provider RPM in offline artifact and verify signatures
- Update proxy config to reference new PKCS#11 URI and restart
- Run handshake smoke tests (see test commands)
- Rollback plan: restore config + old provider RPM

kevin: What are the 'test commands'? We should give 2 quick checks.
sam: Keep two: a TLS handshake test and a connectivity test.
raul: TLS test (uses openssl engine PKCS11 or curl):
```bash
# TLS handshake (shows cert chain)
openssl s_client -connect localhost:443 -servername example.internal -showcerts

# force DNS to resolve to local proxy for connectivity test
curl --resolve example.internal:443:127.0.0.1 https://example.internal/health -v
```

Add a note to use `--resolve` or local /etc/hosts entries for split-DNS.
tess-docs: Nice. Also customers sometimes put the proxy on Windows. Can we add one-liner for Windows TLS passthrough check? Keep it simple.
raul: `Test-NetConnection -ComputerName example.internal -Port 443` and `Get-EventLog -LogName Application -Newest 50` for proxy logs.
devops-bot: CI for PR #4278: docs-linter passed, linkcheck: failed (1 broken link to legacy hsm rotation guide), spellcheck: passed. Details: https://ci.redwood/links/4278
sam: Where's the broken link? I'll patch to point to the new 'hsm-key-rotation-v2.md' anchor.
tess-docs: Also drop a tiny paragraph that clarifies when TLS is terminated at the proxy vs passthrough and the HSM implications (private key usage).
sec: Add a security note: if the HSM enforces non-exportable keys, document how the proxy integrates (engine, pkcs11 provider) and that private keys never leave the HSM.
kevin: Should we include a short example for OpenSSL engine_pkcs11 config? One-liner is fine.
raul: One-liner: `openssl pkcs11 -engine pkcs11 -keyform engine -key 'pkcs11:token=acme;object=bastion-key'` (explain it uses engine to reference key handle).
sam: Great. I'll update the PR with these snippets, the checklist, the verification examples, and the Windows notes. I'll also fix the broken link and rerun CI. Expect an update in ~20m.
devops-bot: CI for PR #4278: linkcheck fixed, all checks passed :white_check_mark:
tess-docs: LGTM, merging after a quick manual review. Thanks all! :shipit:
kevin: Thx team, good to have a concise migration doc for HSM provider swaps.
